How Raised Earnings Guidance Will Impact FedEx Stock
sum: FedEx reported third quarter 2026 sales of US$22,855 million compared with US$20,432 million a year earlier, alongside lower quarterly net income and earnings per share. The company raised full year 2026 revenue and diluted EPS guidance and also expects about 10% revenue growth in the fourth quarter.

The appointment of Jamere Jackson as Chief Financial Officer, following senior finance roles at AutoZone, Hertz, Nielsen and General Electric, adds a seasoned capital allocation voice at a time when FedEx is updating its profit outlook and reporting sharply higher four month earnings.
Attention now turns to how FedEx's upgraded full year earnings guidance may reshape the existing investment narrative built around cost transformation.
Scan FedEx's guidance-led momentum alongside a curated 39 high quality undervalued stocks that pairs robust fundamentals with potential re-rating catalysts.

To own FedEx, you need to believe the cost and technology overhaul can translate solid package demand into steadier earnings and cash generation. The raised full year revenue and EPS guidance, along with an outlook for about 10% Q4 revenue growth, keeps that execution story alive even as quarterly net income and EPS come in lower.

The near term catalyst is still clear delivery on DRIVE and Network 2.0 savings, plus mix shift into higher value verticals such as healthcare and AI related freight. The biggest risk remains volume or pricing pressure in core industrial and international markets, where any renewed softness could blunt the benefit of these programs.

The most relevant update for that thesis is the sharp step up in full year 2026 diluted EPS guidance to US$35.30 to US$35.90 from a prior US$16.55 to US$17.75 range, alongside expected revenue growth of about 12%. That is a significant reset of what management thinks the profit engine can produce, even after adjusting for accounting items flagged in the outlook.

FedEx stock slips as stronger outlook meets cost pressure
sum: FedEx stock was 3.39 percent below the 288.80-euro quote cited in the previous report at 16:34 CET on Thursday, November 5. The move comes as investors weigh the company's higher 2026 earnings outlook against rising operating costs.

The real-time quote of FedEx stock was 279.00 euros on Lang & Schwarz at 17:00 CET on Friday, November 6, 3.56 percent below the Xetra close of Thursday, November 5, at 289.30 euros. The quote was 3.39 percent below the 288.80 euros reported by Ad-Hoc-News on November 5.

FedEx raised its calendar 2026 adjusted diluted earnings outlook to 18.00 to 18.60 U.S. dollars per share from 16.90 to 18.10 U.S. dollars. The company also lifted its revenue-growth forecast to about 12 percent from 11 percent, according to the FedEx newsroom release published on October 28.

For the quarter ended September 30, revenue rose to 22.9 billion U.S. dollars from 20.4 billion dollars a year earlier. Adjusted diluted earnings per share increased to 3.74 U.S. dollars from 2.93 dollars, and adjusted operating margin improved to 5.3 percent from 5.1 percent.

FedEx said higher package yields, stronger volumes and structural cost reductions supported the result. Purchased transportation expense rose 19 percent year over year to 6.455 billion U.S. dollars, while fuel expense increased 64 percent to 1.270 billion dollars. Those costs keep execution and margin expansion central to the investment case.

FedEx completed 2.0 billion U.S. dollars of share repurchases between June and September. The company had 4.3 billion dollars remaining under its 2026 authorization at September 30 and plans to raise parcel shipping rates by an average of 5.9 percent effective January 4, 2027.

FedEx Falls on Disappointing Fiscal Q2 Earnings: ETFs in Focus
sum: After the closing bell on Dec 19, transport bellwether FedEx FDX disappointed investors when it reported its second-quarter fiscal 2024 results. The courier company missed both earnings and revenue estimates and cut the revenue guidance for the fiscal year on an expected drop in demand from the U.S. Postal Service.

Following the results, FDX shares tumbled as much as 9.8% in after-market trade and nearly 10% in pre-market trade at the time of writing. Weak trading is also expected to be felt in the ETF world, especially with respect to the ones with the highest allocation to FedEx. These include ProShares Supply Chain Logistics ETF SUPL, iShares U.S. Transportation ETF IYT, Pacer Industrials and Logistics ETF SHPP and First Trust Nasdaq Transportation ETF FTXR.

Earnings per share came in at $3.99, lagging the Zacks Consensus Estimate of $4.14 but improving from $3.18 reported a year ago. Revenues fell 3% year over year to $22.16 billion and were shy of the estimated $22.33 billion. This marked the fifth quarterly drop in revenues (see: all the Industrials ETFs here).

For fiscal 2024, the shipping giant forecasts revenues to decline by a low-single-digit percentage versus the prior projection of flat numbers. This marked the second consecutive quarter when FedEx lowered its sales view. Management stated that revenues will continue to be dampened by volatile macroeconomic conditions, which will affect customer demand for its services across transportation companies.

ProShares Supply Chain Logistics ETF is the first ETF focused exclusively on the companies poised to benefit from the transformation of how raw materials and goods move around the world. These logistics companies include leading global shipping, railroad, air and trucking companies that collectively touch every point of the supply chain. It follows the FactSet Supply Chain Logistics Index, charging investors 58 bps in annual fees.

ProShares Supply Chain Logistics ETF holds 40 stocks in its basket, with FedEx taking the second spot with 4.6% of the assets. It has amassed $2 million in its asset base and trades in a volume of 300 shares per day. It charges 58 bps in fees per year from investors (read: 5 ETFs to Play Robust Christmas Travel).

FedEx stock holds near USD 296 as earnings date approaches
sum: FedEx Corp. (ISIN US31428X1063) traded at USD 295.51 on the NYSE in pre-market trading at 12:17 p.m. Eastern Time on September 23, 2026, down 0.15 percent from the prior close of USD 295.94. The stock sits between a 52-week low of USD 224.61 and a high of USD 413.87, while its market capitalization is USD 70.00 billion.

The latest operating picture centers on fiscal 2026, which ended May 31, 2026. According to TIKR on September 23, 2026, FedEx generated adjusted free cash flow of USD 4.7 billion in fiscal 2026 and management is targeting USD 6 billion by 2029. That target would be USD 1.3 billion above the fiscal 2026 level, making cash conversion a measurable strategic benchmark.

Capital spending was USD 3.8 billion in fiscal 2026, versus approximately USD 4.3 billion of depreciation and amortization, according to TIKR. The USD 500 million gap indicates that the current investment profile is more restrained than the depreciation burden, a factor that can support near-term cash flow while placing greater importance on network efficiency.

FedEx last reported quarterly results for the quarter ended May 31, 2026. The company reported revenue of USD 23.26 billion and earnings of USD 5.88 per share, according to MarketBeat on September 22, 2026. Net margin for that period was 4.68 percent, providing a clear profitability reference against the cash flow focus.

The next confirmed earnings date is October 28, 2026, according to MarketBeat on September 23, 2026. That report will show whether the USD 23.26 billion quarterly revenue base and USD 5.88 earnings-per-share result are moving in line with the companys cash-conversion ambitions.

At USD 295.51, the stock was USD 118.36 below its 52-week high of USD 413.87 and USD 70.90 above its 52-week low of USD 224.61 on September 23, 2026. The quote was 37.5 percent of the way from the low to the high, while average daily volume was 1.72 million shares.

FedEx stock therefore combines a USD 70.00 billion market value with a recent quarterly revenue base of USD 23.26 billion and fiscal 2026 adjusted free cash flow of USD 4.7 billion. The October 28, 2026 earnings date is the next dated checkpoint for testing that combination.
